name: core--shareurl-page-redesign
description: shareurl.koeff.com is replaced with a redesigned single-file page. The old page was a 2023-era ChatGPT scaffold: alert() for both the error path and the copy confirmation, document.execCommand('copy'), a hard-coded 351px textarea that broke on a phone, an external icons8 sprite fetched on every load, and a regex that matched exactly one URL shape. The new page keeps the same contract — one static document, no build step, no external request, served as an Envoy direct_response — and changes what happens between paste and link. Errors are an inline aria-live status line. Copy is navigator.clipboard with an execCommand fallback and a select-the-text last resort. The parser scans the whole pasted blob rather than a single line, because QuMagie hands out the same share code under three hosts at once (myqnapcloud DDNS, WAN IP, LAN IP) and users paste all three; identical codes dedupe to one result and distinct codes become selectable chips. A myQNAPcloud SmartShare link is recognised by name and rejected with a specific reason, since its code is an obfuscated percent-encoded path with no /sl/ segment to extract. The result is rendered as a card with a QR code generated in-page by a from-scratch encoder (byte mode, ECC L, versions 1-6) so that sharing to a phone needs no CDN and no tracking pixel, plus Copy, Open, the native share sheet where the browser has one, and the last six codes in localStorage

implementation.change: The file is replaced wholesale, 143 lines -> 664 lines, 3905 bytes -> 24329 bytes. It stays the single source for the page: envoy.yaml.j2 inlines it verbatim through lookup('file', 'caddy/nginx/shareurl-index.html') | indent(32, true) into the shareurl virtual host's direct_response, so no task, snippet or default changes and the deploy path is the existing --tags caddy_stack. envoy.yaml.j2 gains exactly one line, max_direct_response_body_size_bytes: 262144 on route_config — Envoy caps direct_response bodies at 4096 bytes and rejects the entire config at load when one is over, which the old 3905-byte page cleared by 191 bytes. Extraction is now a global regex over the whole textarea value, /(?:qumagie\/(?:#\/)?sl\/|\/sl\/)([A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,})/g, which accepts the qumagie/sl/CODE and qumagie/#/sl/CODE forms under any host, port or IP, tolerates a query string and surrounding text, and is idempotent on an already-converted share.koeff.com/sl/CODE. A bare code is accepted only when it is 6+ chars and carries a digit or mixed case. The QR encoder is ~200 lines of the file: GF(256) tables, Reed-Solomon, the six ECC-L version rows, alignment and format placement, all eight masks with the four penalty rules
implementation.supersedes: No prior eval covers the page content. 017 asserted 'shareurl.koeff.com static site is byte-identical between cluster and Caddy (3905 bytes, matching sha)'. That was a switchover parity check against cluster00, which reports/cluster00-decommission-2026-08-16.md is retiring and whose shareurl-v2.koeff.com host already resolves to nothing. 017 stays pass as the record of the switchover; this eval is where the page content lives from now on. helmfile-home-lab/values/common/nginx-url-converter-static-site.yaml.gotmpl still holds the old markup inline for the cluster00 release and is deliberately not touched here — it is a different layer with a different owning tool, and it is being decommissioned rather than kept in sync

checks: STATIC (done): the file contains no {{ or }} and no tab characters, so the indent(32, true) block scalar in envoy.yaml.j2 cannot be broken by its content and no Jinja delimiter can survive into the render
STATIC (done): envoy.yaml.j2 renders against roles/ops-settings/defaults/main.yaml through the role, so lookup('file', ...) resolves against roles/ops-settings/files. 972 lines, 63547 bytes

STATIC (done): the pinned Envoy image, docker.io/envoyproxy/envoy@sha256:574348fa...a45a8, accepts the rendered config under --mode validate — 'configuration OK'. This is the same gate the play applies before compose touches the running stack, and it is what caught the 4096-byte body cap

STATIC (done): no external origin is referenced. No <script src>, <link href> to a CDN, @import, or remote image — the favicon is a data: URI, every icon is inline SVG, and the QR code is drawn on a canvas from a locally computed matrix. The old page's https://img.icons8.com sprite is gone
STATIC (done): no secret value added. The page contains one hostname, share.koeff.com, which is public

RUNTIME (done, local): the rendered config was run in a throwaway Envoy container on 127.0.0.1:18080 and the real response checked, not just the config's validity. GET / with Host: shareurl.koeff.com returns 200, 24329 bytes, byte-identical to the repo file (cmp), content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8 and x-frame-options: SAMEORIGIN. /index.html returns 200, /nope returns 404, and an unmatched Host still returns 200 from the koeff-404 fallback vhost — the path matrix the shareurl vhost had before is unchanged

BEHAVIOUR (done): the four URL shapes the user supplied are exercised as one multi-line paste and individually — the SmartShare link, koeff.myqnapcloud.com:8080/qumagie/sl/iiuB68, 151.251.104.115:8080/qumagie/sl/iiuB68 and 192.168.31.108:8080/qumagie/sl/iiuB68. The blob yields exactly one result, /sl/iiuB68, with no chips; each QuMagie URL alone yields the same; the SmartShare link alone is refused with its own message
BEHAVIOUR (done): two distinct codes in one paste render both as chips with the first active, and an error clears stale chips

BEHAVIOUR (done): the QR code decodes back to the link it encodes, checked with BarcodeDetector rather than by eye, at version 3, 4 and 6. Version 6 is the case that exercises two-block Reed-Solomon interleaving. Over the ECC-L byte ceiling the encoder returns null and the QR tile hides while the link stays

BEHAVIOUR (done): the QR is drawn dark-on-light in both colour schemes. An inverted code is legal in the spec and unreliable in phone cameras, so the --qr-* tokens deliberately do not follow the dark theme
BEHAVIOUR (done): no console error on load or on any of the above paths, at 375px and at desktop width, in light and dark

PENDING (deploy): ansible-playbook -l ops --tags caddy_stack -e caddy_enabled=true against vm700. Not run from this session — the play reads CERT_MANAGER_CLOUDFLARE_TOKEN and the ACME email from the environment, and applying it restarts the sidecar that also serves share.koeff.com
PENDING (post-deploy): https://shareurl.koeff.com/ returns 200 with the new sha and server: envoy, and scripts/migrations/verify_caddy.sh still reports shareurl 200 on both :80 and :443

refutation: REFUTED 'the alert() is the only real problem': document.execCommand('copy') is deprecated and silently no-ops under some engines, and the old copy path reported success unconditionally — the alert claiming 'Copied to clipboard' fired whether or not anything reached the clipboard

REFUTED 'one regex per line is enough': QuMagie presents three URLs for the same share, and the paste people actually make contains all three. Matching the first line only is correct by accident and silently drops the rest

REFUTED 'the SmartShare link can be converted too': its path is a percent-encoded opaque token with no /sl/ segment, so there is no code to extract. It is recognised only so it can be refused with a reason instead of a generic failure

REFUTED 'use a QR library from a CDN': the page is served as an Envoy direct_response with no network dependency of any kind, and adding one would make an offline-capable static page fetch a third-party script on every load

REFUTED 'swapping one static file cannot break the stack': it can, and it did at validate time. A direct_response body over 4096 bytes fails config load outright, so the sidecar that also serves share.koeff.com would have refused to start. The old page cleared that cap by 191 bytes, which is why nothing here had ever needed max_direct_response_body_size_bytes
known_deltas: The QR encoder covers versions 1-6 at ECC L, a 134-byte ceiling. A share link is share.koeff.com/sl/ plus a short code, roughly 34 bytes, so the ceiling is four times the realistic input; past it the QR hides and the link still works
The bare-code heuristic (6+ chars, a digit or mixed case) will convert a plausible-looking word typed on its own. It is a convenience path and the resulting link is visible before it is used
localStorage history is per-browser and unsynced, and is skipped silently in private mode

helmfile-home-lab still carries the old markup for the cluster00 nginx-url-converter release. The two copies now differ by design; the cluster copy serves nothing since the Caddy switchover and is scheduled for decommission

max_direct_response_body_size_bytes is set on route_config, so it lifts the cap for all three inlined pages, not only shareurl. That is the field's scope — it does not exist per route — and 262144 is a bound on what this config may inline, not a target
defects_found_and_fixed_during_validatio: Envoy rejects a direct_response body over 4096 bytes at config load: 'response body size is 24329 bytes; maximum is 4096'. Found by the offline --mode validate run before anything was deployed, which is the failure mode the role's own validate task was written for. Fixed with max_direct_response_body_size_bytes: 262144 on route_config in envoy.yaml.j2
